sources.workflow: Implement mobile-first fluid layouts, container queries, responsive images/navigation and Grid/Flexbox behavior; address overflow, touch targets, viewport height and stacking.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs actual HTML/CSS/components, content and media, target browsers/viewports and an existing design system. Detailed implementation patterns are entirely in an unread reference. No build tooling, browser engine/version, test fixtures or concrete CSS implementation is supplied; real-device checks are explicitly recommended.
sources.offline_assessment: Editing responsive CSS in a real public interface is a legitimate offline source-code task. Standard-library Python can manipulate source text, not compute browser layout or interactions. Without the real project, browser tooling and content there is no verified implementation; synthetic width arithmetic would not demonstrate responsive behavior or hardware usability.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent browser rendering/overflow and keyboard/touch tests across viewport, text-size, language and container-size cases, plus real-device checks. Establish target engine support and compatible build/test dependencies, and check component/media/font/helper licenses before runtime selection.

sources.workflow: Measure portfolio volatility, tail risk, drawdown and risk-adjusted returns across appropriate time horizons, with rolling analysis, stress cases and documented assumptions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a real return/price series, holdings/weights, dates/frequency, costs, risk-free or target-return assumptions, confidence/horizon and lookback choices. The body lists VaR/CVaR, Sharpe/Sortino and other metrics but provides no formulas, implementation, input dataset or pinned numerical dependency; detailed methods are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: Repairing a real public risk-metric implementation against licensed historical data is an actual offline numerical subtask. Some calculations could use standard-library Python, but this body alone cannot fix conventions such as quantiles, annualization or loss signs. No portfolio result, risk-monitoring operation or regulatory adequacy has been established; invented return arrays would not supply missing real-task evidence.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently calculated expected metrics and explicit conventions, with empty/missing data, zero downside variance, heavy tails, drawdowns and stress correlations covered. A finance/domain reviewer must assess assumptions and costs. Verify data/code/helper licenses and any chosen numeric-library compatibility; live portfolio access is not needed for the offline subtask.

sources.workflow: Build Rust async tasks using Tokio futures, channels, cancellation, bounded spawning and tracing, while preserving error propagation and avoiding blocking/locks across awaits.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Quick-start manifest names Tokio 1 with full features, futures 0.3, async-trait 0.1, anyhow 1.0, tracing 0.1 and tracing-subscriber 0.3; requires compatible Rust/Cargo and locally available crates. CancellationToken guidance needs its actual providing dependency resolved. Detailed patterns are unread; no production workload is supplied.
sources.offline_assessment: The included async example is real Rust source, and repairing a public async lifecycle defect is a valid offline code subtask with a complete crate corpus. Standard-library Python supplies neither Rust compilation nor Tokio execution. fetch_data only sleeps and formats a string, so it is explicitly not evidence of network fetching or service behavior.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent compile/type/Send checks and deterministic timeout, cancellation, error and task-bound tests on actual code, with separate load evidence for performance claims. Verify compiler/crate version resolution, missing helper APIs and source/dependency licenses. No Cargo build, network request or performance run occurred.

sources.workflow: Validate web forms, navigation, dialogs and live announcements using actual screen readers in browse/focus modes and multiple desktop/mobile browser combinations.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Minimum stated coverage is NVDA with Firefox on Windows, VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and iOS; broader coverage adds JAWS, TalkBack and Narrator. Needs a real application, test scenarios and assistive-technology/device access. Platform setup is in four unread references. Modal snippets depend on surrounding state/DOM and are not a complete application.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline public-code subtask is repairing actual HTML/ARIA and focus-management code with a local app corpus. Python HTML parsing can inspect markup but cannot prove accessible names, browser focus or spoken announcements; the displayed logger is not a screen-reader oracle. Required cross-platform and mobile experience cannot be established by static review or simulators.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent keyboard/focus regressions and recordings or observations from actual requested screen-reader/browser combinations, including errors and dynamic updates. Specifically verify programmatic heading focus, trap scope and focus restoration instead of trusting the snippet. Confirm assistive-tool licensing, version compatibility and app/helper/content reuse rights.

sources.workflow: Instrument service-mesh metrics, distributed tracing and logs, define golden-signal alerts/SLOs, correlate exemplars and visualize dependency/latency behavior.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a chosen Istio or Linkerd deployment, actual services/traffic and telemetry schemas, propagation/instrumentation, collectors/storage/dashboards and retention/cost requirements. Concrete templates are wholly in an unread reference. Listed threshold examples are not calibrated deployment requirements; compatible mesh and telemetry component versions are unspecified.
sources.offline_assessment: Repairing a real public telemetry configuration or propagation helper against licensed exported traces/metrics is an actual offline subtask. No such code/data is supplied by this body. Standard-library Python may analyze suitable exports, but cannot demonstrate live propagation, SLO alert delivery, mesh connectivity or production storage cost behavior.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independently labeled trace-span relationships, metric/latency/error calculations and sampling/cardinality checks, plus separately controlled end-to-end instrumentation/alert tests. Confirm implementation/helper availability, component compatibility, telemetry privacy and code/data/dependency licenses; observed operational performance remains unproven.

sources.workflow: Define a campaign, draft platform-specific variants, optionally upload media, validate timing, publish/schedule through SocialClaw and retrieve engagement after 24 to 48 hours.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Body declares MIT and explicitly requires SOCIALCLAW_API_KEY plus an active account with connected social accounts and a suitable workspace tier. Setup offers a skill package or socialclaw version 0.1.12 with Node/npm. Needs actual copy, platforms, schedule/timezone, media and platform timing/rate rules; Claude drafting is part of the described workflow, not an action performed here.
sources.offline_assessment: Offline preparation of a real campaign draft or repair of an actual public client schedule validator could be a substantive bounded subtask if its source and inputs are supplied. This body has no client implementation or API schema. Python alone cannot establish service scheduling, connected-account permissions, publishing, media storage or real engagement; stubs would not prove those behaviors.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent content/timing/timezone and payload-contract checks for any actual client code, with compatible SDK/runtime and dependency-license review despite the body MIT declaration. Full publish/analytics claims need separately authorized service receipts and post/time evidence, not placeholder IDs or API-key access during review. The platform count claim also needs reconciliation with the listed table.

sources.workflow: Tune Spark partitioning, adaptive query execution, skew/shuffle, serialization and executor memory; filter/select/aggregate Parquet data and inspect execution metrics.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Example imports PySpark SQL and uses SparkSession/AQE/Kryo configuration with remote object-storage input/output. Full behavior needs compatible Spark/PySpark and JVM, real data/schema/volume, storage connectors and executor resources. Detailed tuning patterns are unread; local licensed dataset, saved plans/event logs and baseline metrics must be provided for an offline task.
sources.offline_assessment: Repairing a real public Spark transformation/configuration and analyzing supplied execution plans is a legitimate offline code subtask; a local Spark workload may later test correctness if its environment exists. Standard-library Python lacks Spark/Parquet execution, and rewriting the aggregation as a toy Python loop would not establish optimization. Cluster scaling, remote storage and speedups are unverified.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent output-equivalence fixtures, measured before/after plans and runtime/resource results on a representative dataset, including skew, spills and partition variation. Confirm Spark/JVM/Python/connector compatibility and source/data/helper/dependency licenses; no session, storage access, overwrite or benchmark was run.

sources.workflow: Select an agent-team size and role preset for task complexity, match each role to tool capability, choose display mode and coordinate nonoverlapping responsibilities.

Related decomposition/communication guidance is unread, and the body gives no independently validated sizing benchmark or implementation.
sources.offline_assessment: Reviewing an actual public team configuration or harness capability manifest could be an offline artifact/code subtask, but none is delivered here. Standard-library Python is not a replacement for the named harness, role tools or display integration. Preset team sizes and tool tables are claims/heuristics, not proof of availability, productivity or runtime eligibility; no team was spawned.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent harness-version/capability checks and task-specific evidence that roles, ownership and permissions match requirements; actual coordination and display claims require separately authorized observation. Check harness/tool/helper licenses and compatibility. Do not treat successful plan writing as evidence of multi-agent execution.

Standard-library Python could inspect structured inventories but cannot demonstrate deployed WAF, EDR, encryption or incident-response effectiveness. Fabricated threats or a toy coverage score would not establish the actual workflow.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Need independent threat-to-control completeness/appropriateness review, explicit scoring assumptions and evidence-linked residual-risk/cost decisions; control-effectiveness claims require separately isolated tests of the real implementation. Confirm inventory/data/helper/implementation licenses and any selected tool compatibility. No security control was deployed or tested.
